title: F7: aggregate reads enumerate every row (adapter test)
outcome: Kabir F7: coarse reads must list every row and field object read
acceptance: Every aggregate/scan adapter is enumerated by the test; each records every row read plus its field objects
A scan that found nothing records no read and the limitation is documented in ADR-05 (absence reads deferred to 2.0)
summary: Review fixes: ADR-05 line now states read_table skips tombstones (deleted-before-scan rows unrecorded, never repaired; point read records them; no v1 adapter calls read_table). Test asserts NO_READ disjoint from AGGREGATE and JOIN.
review:
[kabir · changes] Consistent with CALL-02 'enumerated rows suffice'; 20/20 tests/world pass. Sets-union equality catches an unclassified new adapter; read_table suppliers asserts exact rows+iban; docs.write asserts exact rows+ver/hash. Changes: (1) ADR-05 line understates the limit: read_table skips tombstoned rows, so a row deleted before a scan (e.g. bad crm.delete_customer) is unlisted and the scan's output is not repaired after restore. State it: 'rows absent at scan time, never created or deleted, are not listed; point reads of a deleted row do record its tombstone; no v1 adapter calls read_table, so no F-scenario hits this'. Rows created after a scan are correctly not taint-relevant. (2) Assert NO_READ disjoint from AGGREGATE and JOIN. I will add the matching known-limit line to THREAT-MODEL (claim 7 says 'coarse reads').

[kabir · done] Both changes verified: ADR-05 bullet states tombstone limit accurately (deleted-before-scan unrecorded, never repaired; point read records it; no v1 adapter calls read_table); NO_READ disjointness asserted (line 23). Matching known-limit line added to THREAT-MODEL Errata, wording agrees. tests/world 20 passed.
